images.title: Digital root 5 between 600 and 700
images.purpose: Shows that numbers with the same digital root step up in nines, starting from 608.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no characters, no extra text. One long number line across the centre with eleven evenly spaced dots.
images.exact_structure: A horizontal number line from 600 to 700 with numerals only at 600 and 700 at its ends. Eleven equal reddish purple (#CC79A7) dots on the line at 608, 617, 626, 635, 644, 653, 662, 671, 680, 689 and 698, evenly spaced 9 apart. Numerals under only the first, second and last dots: 608, 617 and 698. Small amber (#E69F00) arcs above the line join each dot to the next, 10 arcs; only the first arc carries the label +9. Above the line, centred: digital root 5. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Adding 9 keeps the digital root, so the numbers with root 5 run 608, 617, ... , 698.
images.description: Shows that numbers with the same digital root step up in nines, starting from 608.

image_decisions.why: Evenly spaced dots in steps of 9 show why each digital root repeats every 9 numbers.
